label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, pool-exhaustion, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 8 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT cents (unchanged), REFUND_CONNECTION kept -> returned); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: pool-exhaustion
case.title: Payments fail: the payments API's database pool runs dry
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the payments API with a connection leak (REFUND_CONNECTION=kept): reading a payment's refunds takes a connection from its database pool of 10 and never gives it back, so after about ten refunds the pool is empty, and every request waits for a connection until the pool's 5 s timeout, then fails with a 500.
case.remedy: roll the payments API back to REFUND_CONNECTION=returned: its new container starts with a full pool

expected_symptoms: the pool runs dry about 40 to 50 s after the deploy; then POST /payments takes 5 to 8 s (a worker thread, then the pool's 5 s wait) and fails with a 500: the p95 latency passes 7 s, and the 5xx share passes 70% within a minute
the payments API logs 'unhandled error' with PoolTimeout: no connection within 5 s
its health check fails too, so docker marks it unhealthy, while PostgreSQL itself is up
the traffic's clients retry and give up: many payments end with their outcome unknown, and arrivals past 64 in flight are shed
the money check passes: a payment that never got a connection was never charged, and one charged before its answer was lost is confirmed by its webhook
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to REFUND_CONNECTION=returned: its new container starts with a full pool

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payments-api deploy at 19:33:24Z exhausted its Postgres connection pool. The likeliest cause is the REFUND_CONNECTION=kept setting: refund requests appear to hold or leak pooled connections instead of returning them. Requests then queue for a connection for about 6 s and fail with psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout. That gives the 500s on POST /payments, which started within about a minute of the deploy, and the p95 of about 7 s. The provider is not the cause: its calls answer in under 20 ms. Redis is also fast. Open questions: I could not see the settings from before the deploy. So I cannot prove that REFUND_CONNECTION (rather than PROVIDER_BREAKER or CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT) is the setting that changed, and I saw no pool-usage metric. CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents may also deserve a money_check after recovery.

evidence.shows: 500s on payments-api appear only in the newest sample (4.6/s at 19:34:33), while 201s drop from about 3.9/s to 1.1/s. This confirms the alert.

payments-api alone was redeployed at 19:33:24Z, about a minute before the 500s, with PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents and REFUND_CONNECTION=kept. Every other container dates from 19:31:58.
The POST /payments errors are all unhandled psycopg_pool PoolTimeout exceptions: the database connection pool is exhausted.
A failing POST /payments trace spends about 5 s between its Redis SET and EVAL waiting for a DB connection (6.3 s in total, error psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout), with no provider call and no DB span.
Refunds before the deploy took 8–16 ms. The one refund after the deploy took 6.35 s.
The p95 of payments-api's calls to the provider stays at 5–19 ms throughout, so provider latency is not holding connections.
The post-deploy refund also failed with PoolTimeout, so the pool is starved for every route of payments-api.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its settings from before the 19:33:24Z deploy, most likely restoring the earlier REFUND_CONNECTION behaviour, so that connections are returned to the pool. Then confirm that the 5xx rate and p95 recover, and run money_check, because CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT and refund handling changed in the same deploy.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so payments and refunds fail briefly (they are mostly failing already). In-flight requests may be cut off. Clients retry with idempotency keys in Redis, which limits duplicates. Any payments or refunds booked wrong under the new settings stay wrong and need a separate repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with the 19:33:24Z settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, REFUND_CONNECTION=kept) and investigate the pool further, for example its size and the connections it holds.
